speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your episodes of dizziness and vertigo. To better understand your condition, how long do these episodes typically last, and do you experience any associated symptoms like hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the position-dependence is very telling. Have these episodes been triggered specifically by changes in head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, and do you feel any twitching or jerking of your limbs during them? Also, have you noticed any recent falls or imbalance when walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Based on your history of sudden, position-dependent vertigo without hearing loss or neurological deficits, this is the most likely diagnosis. I recommend performing a Dix-Hallpike maneuver in the examination room to confirm the presence of nystagmus and definitively diagnose the condition.
